Why Muhammad is a messenger

A lifetime among them

By the tradition he lived forty years among his people before he recited a word of this.

Before the Quran he spent a lifetime among his people: forty years, by the tradition. An orphan, a shepherd, a trader. Then the Quran has him remind them of those years and ask: will you not reason? Bukhari reports what his wife Khadija knew of him: he kept family ties, carried the weak, honoured guests, helped the afflicted. The verse asks people to use what they already know.

﴿قُل لَّوْ شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ مَا تَلَوْتُهُۥ عَلَيْكُمْ وَلَآ أَدْرَىٰكُم بِهِۦ ۖ فَقَدْ لَبِثْتُ فِيكُمْ عُمُرًا مِّن قَبْلِهِۦٓ ۚ أَفَلَا تَعْقِلُونَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

Say, "If Allāh had willed, I would not have recited it to you, nor would He have made it known to you, for I had remained among you a lifetime before it. Then will you not reason?"

Quran · Yunus 10:16

﴿أَلَمْ يَجِدْكَ يَتِيمًا فَـَٔاوَىٰ﴾

Translation of the meaning

Did He not find you an orphan and give [you] refuge?

Quran · Ad-Duha 93:6

You might ask

QuestionWas he even a real person?
AnswerYes. A Syriac chronicle of about 640, attributed to Thomas the Presbyter, mentions the Arabs of Muhammad, within a decade of his death. Later outside writers, such as Sebeos, mention him too.Quran · Aal Imran 3:144
QuestionDidn't his opponents call him a liar?
AnswerAfter his call, yes, and the Quran records it. Of the years before, Bukhari reports Abu Sufyan, then his opponent, saying, when questioned, that they had not accused him of lying.Quran · Sad 38:4
QuestionCan't an honest man still be mistaken?
AnswerHe can, and honesty alone settles nothing. It weakens one explanation: a man lying for himself. What remains is yours to weigh.Quran · Yunus 10:16

He asked the people who knew him best to think about what they knew.
